newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Brent/Dubai stays wide in Asia, Tapis paper firm.
newsitem.headline: Brent/Dubai stays wide in Asia, Tapis paper firm.

text.p: Near-month Brent/Dubai paper was firm on Thursday following overnight deals on December.
Meanwhile, paper Tapis was also firm with wet assessments at post Gulf War highs.
Brent/Dubai for November was assessed at a wide $2.20/$2.35, out from $2.01/$2.06 in New York late on Wednesday.
December Brent/Dubai was assessed at $2.08/$2.18, out from New York's $1.95/$2.00.
Overnight, two majors exchanged December Brent/Dubai at $2.10 and a U.S. trader did an in-house deal at $2.15, traders said.
February Brent/Dubai paper was traded at $1.78 between a Wall Street trader and a European major and at the same price between a U.S. trader and a European major.

A February/April Dubai spread was also traded at 78 cents between a European major and a U.S. refiner, while a December/February Dubai intermonth spread was traded at 85 cents between two U.S. traders.

Dubai spreads for November/December and December/January were assessed around 37 cents, in from a day-earlier 41 cents, which traders attributed to the market tightening ahead of India's November crude purchase by tender which closes later on
Thursday. Offers should be valid until Friday.
October paper Tapis was assessed at $23.20/$23.40 while November was assessed at $23.00/$23.20, higher than Wednesday's levels of $23.15/$23.45 and $22.85/$23.10 respectively.
Strong demand for light sweet crudes has been supporting Tapis for several weeks and the global crude rally has further underpinned its value, traders said.
A producer was offering physical October barrels at a fixed price of $24.00/$24.10 or on a market premium basis of $1.40/$1.50.
The fixed price represents the highest level since the Gulf War, when the crude for near-month loading was assessed as high as $39.08 per barrel.
Brokers said first-quarter Tapis traded at $22.12, while an October/November Tapis spread was traded between a major and a Wall Street trader at 21 cents.
